Building blocks for the Coherent GT check, for node 6.18
Researched 2026-10-18 for the architecture plan's node 6.18, the build, on decision 031's open items:
the check tool's parser, its list of banned built-ins and web APIs with an exception for a package's own fill-in,
and whether it also offers an ESLint config; plus the framework's for-of rewrite and naming a source line through a map.
Inputs read first: decisions 030 and 031, record/areas/architecture/coherent-gt.md, the spine's "Compiling our code in
the sim" and "The check", the architecture log's p09 entry, experiments/areas/architecture/p09-coherent-syntax.mjs,
and its results files p09-coherent-syntax-2026-10-09-19-07-30.txt and p09-compilers-2026-10-09-19-30-30.txt.
Development machine: Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200, Node v22.23.1, npm 10.9.8. Nothing here touched the sim or its inspector.
Packages, each the version npm tagged latest on 2026-10-18 unless noted:
  acorn 8.19.0, acorn-walk 8.3.5, espree 11.2.0, meriyah 7.4.0, @eslint-community/regexpp 4.12.2, eslint-scope 9.1.2,
  source-map-js 1.2.2, esbuild 0.28.2, @microsoft/msfs-sdk 2.3.3 (published 2025-12-12), @microsoft/msfs-ts-transformer
  1.0.0, eslint 10.13.0, eslint-plugin-es-x 10.1.0 (with eslint-type-tracer 0.5.2), typescript-eslint 8.71.2,
  typescript 7.0.2 (latest) and 6.0.3, and typescript 5.8.3 for running the transformer.
Evidence markers follow writing.md: measured (we ran it), read (we read it in a package's files or source),
documented (a vendor page says so), unverified (inference, forum post, or guess).
Paths: <scratch> is this session's scratch folder, outside the repository, which holds the scripts and bundles named below;
none of them is committed.

======================================================================
ANSWERS
======================================================================

Q  | Question                                       | Answer
---+------------------------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------
1  | Does acorn at ecmaVersion 2017 reject what     | Yes. Of p09's 45 samples it rejects all 20 the engine fails, and accepts
   | the engine rejects, and accept ES2015-2017?    | all 22 from ES2015 to ES2017. It also rejects 3 the engine parses:
   |                                                | object rest, the template literal revision, and import(). It rejects a
   |                                                | raw U+2028 and U+2029, every ES2018+ regex feature, and the s, d, and v
   |                                                | flags (measured). espree 11.2.0 gives the same verdict on all 65 samples;
   |                                                | meriyah 7.4.0 has no version option and accepted every one (measured).
1b | Validating new RegExp("...", "...") at 2017    | @eslint-community/regexpp's RegExpValidator({ ecmaVersion: 2017 }),
   |                                                | validateFlags then validatePattern: a public API with a version option.
   |                                                | acorn's own validator isn't exported, and building a literal from the
   |                                                | string needs escaping of "/" and line terminators. All three agreed on
   |                                                | 19 patterns (measured). esbuild 0.28.2 at es2017 emits
   |                                                | new RegExp("(?<y>\\d{4})"), plain and minified, and regexpp fails it with
   |                                                | "Invalid group" (measured).
2  | Finding banned built-ins and web APIs, and     | eslint-scope's unresolved references for globals, a member check on those
   | their false-positive cost in a framework bundle| for statics, property names for prototype methods. An FSComponent page on
   |                                                | msfs-sdk 2.3.3, bundled at es2017 (2,535,217 bytes): 0 hits for every
   |                                                | banned name. The whole framework kept (3,689,065 bytes): 2 hits, both
   |                                                | false positives, ArrayUtils.flatMap(...), the framework's own static
   |                                                | helper; 0 real uses, 0 typeof guards, 0 regex problems (measured).
2b | What "an exception for a package's own         | Five rules: a definition isn't a use; a guard isn't a use; a receiver the
   | fill-in" needs                                 | file binds to its own class or object declaring that member isn't the
   |                                                | built-in; a file that installs a fill-in for X passes its uses of X; and
   |                                                | what's left goes in the data file as allowed receivers or source paths,
   |                                                | not as comments, which a minified bundle drops. The framework fills in
   |                                                | nothing: it defines ArrayUtils.at, flat, flatMap, ObjectUtils.fromEntries,
   |                                                | StringUtils.trimStart, and a Warning.description getter (read).
3  | eslint-plugin-es-x 10.1.0's coverage           | Every syntax and regex item of the reference, regex rules included in
   |                                                | RegExp(...) and new RegExp(...) with constant strings, and every ES
   |                                                | built-in but Intl, which no rule bans, and FinalizationRegistry, which only
   |                                                | no-weakrefs bans, with WeakRef, which the engine has (read, measured).
   |                                                | No web APIs: core no-restricted-globals and no-restricted-properties do
   |                                                | those, with no typeof exemption and no window.X (measured).
   |                                                | Prototype methods: by default only receivers its in-file tracer types
   |                                                | (0 of 7 untyped reported); aggressive reports unknown receivers (7 of 7)
   |                                                | and also a local class's own at() and description; typed linting through
   |                                                | typescript-eslint uses TypeScript's types (measured).
3b | An ESLint plugin and config as our tool,       | Feasible, at a cost: about 3x slower (CLI median 1,358ms against 458ms on
   | against a standalone acorn tool                | the 2.5 MB bundle, 1,945ms against 690ms on 3.7 MB), 80 packages and
   |                                                | 12.2 MB against 9 and 1.4 MB, the bundle's 263 eslint-disable comments
   |                                                | to neutralize, and restrict-to-es2017's iterator-helper rules, which in
   |                                                | aggressive mode put 172 false positives on the 2.5 MB bundle (measured).
   |                                                | Editor warnings in TypeScript sources need the TypeScript 6 API beside
   |                                                | TypeScript 7: typescript-eslint 8.71.2 throws "typescript-eslint does not
   |                                                | support TS 7.0." (measured).
4  | @microsoft/msfs-ts-transformer 1.0.0           | Rewrites a for-of over any type with a number index and a numeric length
   |                                                | (arrays, readonly arrays, typed arrays, strings) into an _i_N index loop,
   |                                                | when the body is a block, an expression statement, or empty; and array
   |                                                | destructuring without rest or defaults over such types. It leaves Map, Set,
   |                                                | generators, .values(), any, for await, spread, and an unbraced if as body
   |                                                | (read, measured with TypeScript 5.8.3). msfssdk.js 2.3.3 already holds 109
   |                                                | rewritten loops and 140 for-of it couldn't rewrite; the 2.5 MB bundle keeps
   |                                                | 53 and 94, all from the framework (measured). No measurement of for-of's
   |                                                | cost in Coherent GT found anywhere (unverified).
5  | Naming the source line of a failure in a bundle| esbuild's sourcemap (external or linked) and source-map-js 1.2.2's
   |                                                | originalPositionFor: a named group at bad.js line 54963 maps to
   |                                                | example/bad.ts:8:13, plain and minified; 58ms for the first lookup on a
   |                                                | 5.6 MB map, then 2ms per 1,000 (measured). esbuild chains the framework's
   |                                                | own map, which leads to its compiled build/*.js, not its TypeScript.

Recommended shape:
- A standalone Node CLI on acorn, acorn-walk, eslint-scope, @eslint-community/regexpp, and source-map-js:
  9 packages with their dependencies, 1.4 MB, the five named under MIT and BSD licenses, and under 0.5s on the
  2.5 MB bundle including Node's start.
- It reads one JSON data file holding the reference's lists, checks each file we ship (esbuild's bundles with their maps,
  and hand-written panel JavaScript), and prints file:line:column, then the source file:line:column through the map,
  then the source line from the map's sourcesContent.
- It applies the five exception rules of 2b, under which the framework bundle's 2 false positives would pass with no
  allow-list entry (rule 3).
- It parses at 2017 and lives with the 3 false rejections of section 1 (object rest, template literal revision,
  import()), since esbuild lowers object rest, and neither of the other two appears in the framework's bundles.
- The ESLint config is an optional second export of the same repository, generated from the same data file, with eslint
  and eslint-plugin-es-x as optional peer dependencies the CLI never loads.
  For TypeScript sources it needs only the regex rules and the web-API, Intl, FinalizationRegistry, and crypto.subtle
  bans, since tsc with lib ES2017 already fails every later built-in and esbuild lowers the later syntax.
  It can wait: the after-edit hook that decision 031 asks for gives the same findings, mapped to the TypeScript line,
  within about 0.7s of a save (esbuild about 0.2s plus the check), without the TypeScript 6 install.

======================================================================
1. PARSER
======================================================================

Method (measured): <scratch>/cgt/parse-samples.mjs reads the SYNTAX array straight out of p09-coherent-syntax.mjs and
the engine's verdicts out of p09's 19-07-30 results file, adds 20 samples p09 didn't have, and parses each with
acorn.parse(src, { ecmaVersion: 2017, sourceType, allowReturnOutsideFunction: true }), the same at 2018 and "latest",
espree.parse at 2017 with ecmaFeatures.globalReturn, and meriyah.parse with globalReturn and validateRegex.
p09's samples are function bodies for new Function, hence allowReturnOutsideFunction.
Engine column: p09 on MSFS 2024, 2026-10-09, the same verdict in all five documents (+ parses and returns the value,
x doesn't parse, ! parses and throws when run).

acorn 2017's messages, verbatim, each with line:column in the sample:
  object rest / spread, for await, async generators, optional catch binding, ?., ??, logical assignment,
  class fields, static blocks, dynamic import, import.meta, export * as ns: "Unexpected token (1:N)"
  named groups, lookbehind: "Invalid regular expression: /(?<y>\d{4})/: Invalid group (1:8)"
  unicode properties: "Invalid regular expression: /\p{L}/: Invalid escape (1:8)"
  s, d, and v flags: "Invalid regular expression flag (1:8)"
  template literal revision: "Bad character escape sequence (1:56)"
  U+2028 and U+2029 in a string: "Unterminated string constant (1:7)"
  BigInt literals, numeric separators: "Identifier directly after number (1:16)" and "(1:8)"
  #private fields and methods, #x in obj, hashbang: "Unexpected character '#' (1:10)"
  top-level await: "Cannot use keyword 'await' outside an async function (1:0)"
The error is a SyntaxError with loc.line and loc.column (0-based); acorn stops at the first one, so the check reports
one syntax failure per file.

What the table settles (measured):
- acorn 8.19.0 at 2017 agrees with the engine on 42 of p09's 45 samples, and never accepts what the engine rejects.
- The 3 it gets wrong it gets wrong the safe way: object rest, the template literal revision, and import(), which the
  engine parses (import() wasn't run).
  esbuild at es2017 lowers object rest (into its __objRest helper), so a bundle never carries it.
  It leaves a tagged template with an invalid escape (t`\unicode`) and an external import("./x.js") as written, so a
  bundle with either would fail the check though the engine parses it; neither appears in the framework's bundles
  below, which parse at 2017 with no error.
- The s and d flags, which the engine parses and then throws on when the regex runs, fail the parse, as they should.
- espree 11.2.0 depends on acorn ^8.16.0 and gave acorn's verdict on all 65 samples, with the position moved out of the
  message into lineNumber and column; it adds nothing a standalone tool needs.
- meriyah 7.4.0's Options type has sourceType, next, ranges, webcompat, loc, raw, impliedStrict, preserveParens,
  lexical, jsx, validateRegex, module, and globalReturn, and no ECMAScript version (read in
  dist/types/options.d.ts), so it can't refuse later syntax; it accepted all 65.

Validating the string arguments of new RegExp (measured, <scratch>/cgt/regex-ways.mjs, 19 patterns):
  1. regexpp: new RegExpValidator({ ecmaVersion: 2017 }); validateFlags(flags); then
     validatePattern(pattern, 0, pattern.length, { unicode: flags.includes("u") }).
     Its errors read "Invalid regular expression: /(?<y>\d{4})/: Invalid group" and "Invalid flag 's'", and carry
     the index within the pattern. Its option list names 2018 as adding the s flag, named groups, lookbehind, and
     unicode property escapes, and 2022 the d flag (read in index.d.ts). ESLint and es-x depend on it.
  2. Build a regex literal from the string and parse it with acorn at 2017: works, but the string's cooked value must
     have "/" outside a class and every line terminator escaped first, and the error's position is in the made-up
     literal.
  3. acorn's own validator: RegExpValidationState isn't among acorn's exports (read in dist/acorn.mjs); reaching it
     through a parser's regexpState.constructor works today and could break in any release.
  All three agreed on all 19 patterns, failing named groups, lookbehind and negative lookbehind, \p{L} with u, the s,
  d, and v flags, "gg", "(", and "a{2,1}", and passing \p{L} and \k without u (Annex B), "a/b", a pattern holding a
  newline or U+2028, "[/]", \u{61} with u, and "gimuy".
  Choose 1.
  The check applies it to every RegExp(...) or new RegExp(...) whose callee is the unshadowed global RegExp, with a
  string literal or a template literal without expressions as either argument; a regex literal as the first argument
  carries its own flags, which acorn already checked.
  The framework's 8 RegExp calls are all new RegExp(/literal/i) (read in the bundle), which pass.

esbuild 0.28.2 at es2017 (measured, <scratch>/cgt/esbuild-lowering.mjs and bundle-bad.mjs):
  /(?<y>\d{4})/       -> new RegExp("(?<y>\\d{4})")      regexpp 2017: Invalid group
  /(?<=x)y/           -> new RegExp("(?<=x)y")           Invalid group
  /a.b/s              -> new RegExp("a.b", "s")          Invalid flag 's'
  /a/d                -> new RegExp("a", "d")            Invalid flag 'd'
  /\p{L}/u            -> new RegExp("\\p{L}", "u")       Invalid escape
  /[\p{L}--a]/v       -> new RegExp("[\\p{L}--a]", "v")  Invalid flag 'v'
  10n                 -> /* @__PURE__ */ BigInt("10"), with the warning "Big integer literals are not available in the
                         configured target environment ("es2017") and may crash at run-time"; the check's global
                         BigInt rule catches the call.
  None of the regex rewrites warns, and each output parses at acorn 2017.
  Minified, the bundle keeps the call: let s=new RegExp("(?<y>\\d{4})-(?<m>\\d{2})").exec(...), which the check
  failed at 4:659250 and mapped to example/bad.ts:8:13.
  A raw U+2028 in a string comes out as \u2028 with charset ascii and utf8, minified or not, so in our bundles only
  hand-written JavaScript or tsc's output can carry one.

======================================================================
2. BANNED BUILT-INS AND WEB APIS
======================================================================

How to find uses (measured with the scratch prototype <scratch>/cgt/check.mjs and its banned.json, a copy of the
reference's lists):
- Globals (BigInt, globalThis, AggregateError, FinalizationRegistry, Intl, and the 10 missing web API globals):
  eslint-scope 9.1.2's analyze(ast, { ecmaVersion: 2017, sourceType: "script" }), then globalScope.through, the
  references no scope resolved, minus names a script declares at its top level (globalScope.set), which eslint-scope
  leaves in through.
  This skips a shadowed name: var globalThis = 1 and a parameter named Intl gave no hit.
  eslint-scope reads node.range, which acorn adds only with ranges: true; without it analyze threw "Cannot read
  properties of undefined (reading '0')" in FunctionScope.__isValidResolution.
  Writing our own scope tracking on acorn-walk would redo var hoisting, function and class names, catch parameters,
  and block scopes, which eslint-scope already does, with 4 dependencies (esrecurse, estraverse, and 2 type packages).
- Through a global object: window.X, self.X, and globalThis.X, where X is a banned global (window.queueMicrotask hit).
- Statics: a member whose object is one of those unresolved global identifiers, against the list (Object.fromEntries,
  Object.hasOwn, Promise.any, Promise.allSettled, crypto.subtle).
- Prototype methods (flat, flatMap, at, findLast, toSorted, matchAll, replaceAll, trimStart, finally, description):
  without types, only by property name, on a non-computed member or a computed one with a string literal.
- Error cause: new Error(...) or new XxxError(...) with an object literal second argument that has a cause key.
- Guards: an enclosing typeof, or an if, ternary, or && whose test names the same identifier.
  The prototype misses a few cases the real tool should cover: the test's own read (if (Array.prototype.flat) counted as
  a use), window.crypto.subtle, an alias (var O = Object; O.fromEntries), and destructuring (var { fromEntries } =
  Object). es-x catches the alias and the destructuring (section 3).
  eslint-utils' ReferenceTracker, which es-x uses for that, declares a peer dependency on eslint (read:
  @eslint-community/eslint-utils 4.10.1, peerDependencies eslint "^6.0.0 || ^7.0.0 || >=8.0.0"), so a standalone tool
  follows const aliases itself or leaves them out.

The bundles (measured, <scratch>/cgt/bundle.mjs): esbuild 0.28.2, bundle, format iife, target es2017,
jsxFactory FSComponent.buildComponent, sourcemap external.
- banner.js: a small FSComponent page (example/banner.tsx) using EventBus, Clock, SimVarPublisher, Subject,
  MappedSubject, ConsumerSubject, ArraySubject, NumberFormatter, DisplayComponent, and FSComponent.render, from
  @microsoft/msfs-sdk 2.3.3: 2,535,217 bytes, 55,143 lines (883,159 minified). The framework doesn't tree-shake much.
- whole.js: import * as sdk from "@microsoft/msfs-sdk" put on window, so every export stays: 3,689,065 bytes,
  82,243 lines (1,358,698 minified).
- The published msfssdk-iife.js 2.3.3 itself: 4,795,980 bytes.
- bad.ts: banner's imports plus a named group, peers.flat().at(-1), and new ResizeObserver, as a positive control.
All four parse at acorn 2017, and the published msfssdk.js parses at 2017 as a module.

Hits (measured):

File               | Hits | Names                                            | Real uses | False positives
-------------------+------+--------------------------------------------------+-----------+------------------------------
banner.js          | 0    | none of the 31 names                             | 0         | 0
whole.js           | 2    | prototype flatMap 2                              | 0         | 2: ArrayUtils.flatMap([...]),
                   |      |                                                  |           | in the framework's
                   |      |                                                  |           | autopilot/vnav/VNavEvents.js:75
                   |      |                                                  |           | and lnav/LNavObsEvents.js:26
msfssdk-iife.js    | 2    | prototype flatMap 2                              | 0         | the same 2
bad.ts bundle      | 3+1  | ResizeObserver, flat, at, and the named group    | 4         | 0
None of the bundles has a typeof guard or any other guard around a banned name, and none has a regex problem.

Plain text in whole.js, word-bounded, to show what an AST check rightly skips (measured, textcount.mjs, context.mjs):
  fromEntries 2 (a JSDoc line, "Object.fromEntries is not available in CoherentJS.", and the static method ObjectUtils
  .fromEntries), flat 3 (the static ArrayUtils.flat and 2 comments about "the flat segment"), flatMap 3 (its definition
  and the 2 calls above), description 6 (5 comments and Warning's getter), finally 2 (a comment and a try ... finally),
  trimStart 1 (StringUtils.trimStart), cause 7 (all comments), at 461 (the English word, in comments or strings; none as .at), RegExp 8,
  and 0 for every other name: globalThis, BigInt, Intl, the web APIs, hasOwn, allSettled, subtle, matchAll, findLast,
  toSorted, and replaceAll.
Definitions of a banned name in whole.js (measured, definitions.mjs, sources through the map):
  static ArrayUtils.at       utils/datastructures/ArrayUtils.js:52   (never called in the framework)
  static ArrayUtils.flatMap  utils/datastructures/ArrayUtils.js:152
  static ArrayUtils.flat     utils/datastructures/ArrayUtils.js:176
  static ObjectUtils.fromEntries  utils/datastructures/ObjectUtils.js:11
  get Warning.description    components/Warnings/Warning.js:49
  static StringUtils.trimStart    utils/strings/StringUtils.js:26
  Paths are the framework's build folder as its own source map names it.
So the framework 2.3.3 fills in no built-in: it ships its own helpers under its own names, and the only cost of a
property-name check on it is the 2 ArrayUtils.flatMap calls.
Our code would add more of the same kind: ArrayUtils.at(arr, -1), StringUtils.trimStart(s), or warning.description
would each be flagged by name (unverified count; we wrote no such code here).

What "an exception for a package's own fill-in" needs (a design sketch from the cases above, not built):
  1. A definition isn't a use: class members and object keys (the AST check already skips them), assignment targets
     such as Array.prototype.flat = function () {...}, Object.defineProperty(Array.prototype, "flat", ...), and a
     top-level function ResizeObserver() {} in a script, which scope analysis already resolves.
  2. A guard isn't a use: typeof X, "flat" in Y, or Y.flat read in an if, ternary, or && test; and the guarded branch,
     as in typeof ResizeObserver !== "undefined" ? new ResizeObserver(cb) : null, passes too.
  3. A receiver the file binds to its own class or object that declares the member isn't the built-in: ArrayUtils
     resolves to var ArrayUtils = class _ArrayUtils { ... static flatMap(array, map) { ... } } at whole.js line 8044,
     in the same bundle. This clears both framework hits.
  4. A file that installs a fill-in for X, by rule 1's assignments or defineProperty, passes its own uses of X, and
     the report lists the fill-in by its source path. Whether a use can run before the fill-in, through esbuild's
     module order, isn't checked (unverified).
  5. What's left goes in the data file: receiver names (the sim's own copy, msfssdk.ArrayUtils.flatMap, resolves to
     nothing in the file) and source paths matched through the map (for example @microsoft/msfs-sdk/**), each with
     a reason. Not as comments in the code: esbuild keeps comments in a plain bundle (263 of the framework's
     eslint-disable lines reached banner.js) and drops them when it minifies (0 in banner.min.js).
  The data file also keeps "filled in in some documents" apart from "missing", so the message can say which
  documents have the fill-in, though both fail.

The reference is a sample: the check passes a later built-in the reference doesn't name, such as findLastIndex,
trimEnd, toReversed, Object.groupBy, or Promise.withResolvers (unverified whether the engine lacks each).
In TypeScript sources, tsc with lib ES2017 fails those; in JavaScript files and packages, nothing does.
TypeScript's lib.es2021.weakref.d.ts declares FinalizationRegistry beside WeakRef (read in typescript 6.0.3), so the
type check passes FinalizationRegistry, which the engine lacks; the check's list has to hold it, and does.

Timing of the prototype in process (measured): banner.js parse 215ms, eslint-scope 78ms, walk 44ms; whole.js 288ms,
127ms, 61ms; msfssdk-iife.js 290ms, 119ms, 65ms.

======================================================================
3. ESLINT-PLUGIN-ES-X
======================================================================

eslint-plugin-es-x 10.1.0 has 373 rules; its flat/restrict-to-es2017 config turns on 109 (read by loading the plugin,
<scratch>/cgt/esx-list.mjs). It requires eslint >=10.6.0 and Node ^22.23.0 || ^24.18.0 || >=26.4.0 (read in its
package.json), and depends on @eslint-community/regexpp, @eslint-community/eslint-utils, and eslint-type-tracer.

The reference's items against its rules (read; each in restrict-to-es2017 unless noted):
  Object spread                   no-rest-spread-properties, which bans object rest too (the engine parses rest)
  for await, async generators     no-async-iteration
  Optional catch binding          no-optional-catch-binding
  Named groups, lookbehind        no-regexp-named-capture-groups, no-regexp-lookbehind-assertions
  Unicode property escapes        no-regexp-unicode-property-escapes (and its -2019 to -2023 variants)
  s, d (and v) flags              no-regexp-s-flag, no-regexp-d-flag, no-regexp-v-flag
  Raw U+2028, U+2029 in a string  no-json-superset
  ?., ??, ||= &&= ??=             no-optional-chaining, no-nullish-coalescing-operators, no-logical-assignment-operators
  BigInt literals and BigInt      no-bigint
  Numeric separators              no-numeric-separators
  Class fields                    no-class-instance-fields, no-class-static-fields (no-class-fields exists, not in it)
  #private fields and methods     no-class-private-fields, no-class-private-methods
  Static blocks, #x in obj        no-class-static-block, no-private-in
  (Template literal revision, import(): no-malformed-template-literals, no-dynamic-import, both of which the engine
   parses)
  flat, flatMap                   no-array-prototype-flat
  Object.fromEntries              no-object-fromentries
  Symbol.prototype.description    no-symbol-prototype-description
  globalThis                      no-global-this
  matchAll                        no-string-prototype-matchall
  Promise.any, AggregateError     no-promise-any
  FinalizationRegistry            only no-weakrefs, which bans WeakRef too; the engine has WeakRef
  Array and String at             no-array-prototype-at, no-string-prototype-at
  Object.hasOwn                   no-object-hasown
  findLast                        no-array-prototype-findlast-findlastindex
  toSorted                        no-array-prototype-tosorted
  Intl                            no rule: its Intl rules ban later Intl APIs only
  Error cause                     no-error-cause
  Promise.prototype.finally       no-promise-prototype-finally
  Promise.allSettled              no-promise-all-settled
  trimStart                       no-string-prototype-trimstart-trimend
  replaceAll                      no-string-prototype-replaceall
  The 11 missing web APIs         no rule; core no-restricted-globals and no-restricted-properties (crypto.subtle)

Regex features inside new RegExp: its regex rules walk ReferenceTracker's RegExp calls and constructions and read each
argument with getStringIfConstant (read in dist/index.mjs, the generator over RegExp calls in its lib/utils.ts region),
so they cover RegExp("...") and new RegExp("...", "...") with string literals, and go further than our fixed string by
resolving constant variables (read, not measured).
On sample files they failed new RegExp("(?<y>\\d{4})"), new RegExp("a.b", "s"), RegExp("\\p{L}", "u"), and
new RegExp("(?<=x)y") (measured).

Prototype methods, with and without types (measured on example/unknown.js and tsel/src/page.ts):
- Default: a rule reports only when eslint-type-tracer, which reads the current file only, proves the receiver's type:
  [1, [2]].flat(), "abc".at(-1), Symbol("x").description, and Promise.resolve().finally(...) were reported;
  arr.flat(), arr.at(-1), s.replaceAll(...), s.trimStart(), p.finally(...), sym.description, and utils.flatMap(...) on
  parameters were not: 0 of 7.
- aggressive: true (per rule or settings["es-x"].aggressive) reports a receiver it can't type: 7 of 7. It still left
  ArrayUtils.flatMap alone when ArrayUtils was a local object literal or the framework's class, and reported t.at(0)
  and t.description on an instance of a local class that declares both.
- With typescript-eslint and projectService, it reads TypeScript's types: rows.flat(), rows.at(-1),
  name?.replaceAll(...), p.finally(...), and sym.description were reported without aggressive.
- allowTestedProperty: true lets a guarded property through: Array.prototype.flat ? arr.flat() : arr and
  if (typeof Object.fromEntries === "function") passed, while var O = Object; O.fromEntries([]) and
  var { fromEntries } = Object were still reported. no-global-this has no such option, and core no-restricted-globals
  reported typeof ResizeObserver as a use.

What it leaves out (read, measured): web APIs entirely; Intl; FinalizationRegistry apart from WeakRef; crypto.subtle;
window.X through no-restricted-globals (window.queueMicrotask passed); a typeof guard on a global; the difference
between missing and filled in in some documents; and any exception for a package's own fill-in beyond what its type
tracer infers.

On the bundles (measured, eslint-run.mjs, ESLint 10.13.0, lintText):
  Config                                                    | banner.js 2.5 MB        | whole.js 3.7 MB
  ----------------------------------------------------------+-------------------------+------------------------
  restrict-to-es2017 minus no-weakrefs, plus core bans,      | 0 messages              | 0 messages
  110 rules, default                                        |                         |
  the same, aggressive                                      | 172, all false          | 240, all false
                                                            | positives               | positives
  only the reference's 37 es-x rules plus 2 core rules,     | 0                       | 0
  default or aggressive                                     |                         |
  The 172 on banner.js: Iterator.prototype.map 60, forEach 37, reduce 21, filter 17, find 11, every 4, some 2,
  Set.prototype.intersection 15, and Array.prototype.with 5, such as this.subs.filter(...) and this.with(data, next).
  restrict-to-es2017 bans ES2025's iterator helpers by method name, so with aggressive every .map and .filter on an
  untyped receiver is flagged; a generated config must list only the reference's rules.
  The bundle carries the framework's eslint-disable comments for rules nobody loads (177 jsdoc/require-jsdoc,
  44 jsdoc/require-returns, 38 @typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars, 1 @typescript-eslint/no-non-null-assertion in
  banner.js), and each became an error, "Definition for rule 'jsdoc/require-jsdoc' was not found.", until the
  config set linterOptions.noInlineConfig, which then warns on each that it "has no effect".
  ESLint gave a double message where an es-x rule and a core rule overlap (Promise.allSettled, Object.fromEntries,
  BigInt), so a generated config picks one of the two.

Speed (measured, time.ps1: wall clock, Node's start included, median of 5 runs; ESLint CLI with the reference-only,
aggressive config; the acorn check is <scratch>/cgt/check.mjs):
  File                 | acorn check | ESLint CLI
  ---------------------+-------------+-----------
  banner.js 2.5 MB     | 458ms       | 1,358ms
  whole.js 3.7 MB      | 690ms       | 1,945ms
  banner.min.js 0.9 MB | 405ms       | 1,250ms
  In process, after its first run, ESLint's lintText took between 0.96s and 2.1s on banner.js across our runs,
  against the acorn check's 337ms (parse, scope, and walk).
Dependencies (measured, fresh installs): acorn, acorn-walk, eslint-scope, @eslint-community/regexpp, and source-map-js
are 9 packages and 1.4 MB; eslint, eslint-plugin-es-x, and source-map-js are 80 packages and 12.2 MB.
Licenses (read on npm): acorn, acorn-walk, regexpp, and eslint-plugin-es-x MIT; eslint-scope BSD-2-Clause;
source-map-js BSD-3-Clause; meriyah ISC.

Editor warnings in TypeScript sources (measured in <scratch>/tsel):
- typescript-eslint 8.71.2 declares typescript ">=4.8.4 <6.1.0" as its peer, npm refused the install beside
  typescript 7.0.2 without --legacy-peer-deps, and with it ESLint stopped with "typescript-eslint does not support
  TS 7.0." from typescript-eslint's dist/index.js.
- typescript 7.0.2's package exports only ./lib/version.cjs, ./package.json, and ./unstable/* entries, no compiler
  API (read with npm view).
  TypeScript's announcement says 7.0 ships without an API, and points tools such as typescript-eslint to a
  compatibility package installed as typescript, typescript@npm:@typescript/typescript6, with 7.0 beside it under
  another alias (documented, devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/announcing-typescript-7-0/, "Running side by side with
  TypeScript 6.0").
- With typescript 6.0.3 in its place, a config of the 3 regex rules, no-bigint, 5 prototype-method rules, and
  no-restricted-globals for ResizeObserver and Intl warned on page.ts as expected, untyped and typed: the named group,
  lookbehind, s flag, ResizeObserver, Intl, and 10n; plus the 5 prototype methods when aggressive or typed.
  It didn't warn on ?., ??, a class field, or a #private field, whose rules the config left off because esbuild
  lowers them.
- So in TypeScript sources an ESLint config adds only what tsc's own check misses: the lookbehind, which TypeScript
  7.0.2 didn't flag in p09's compilers run while it flagged named groups and the s flag; the regex features that run
  didn't try (unicode property escapes, the d and v flags; unverified whether tsc flags them); the web APIs, Intl,
  FinalizationRegistry, and crypto.subtle. In hand-written JavaScript, it would carry every rule.

An ESLint plugin as the tool itself: feasible, as one generated flat config of es-x rules plus core rules, with a CLI
wrapper that runs ESLint on our bundles and maps each message through the source map. It would still need rules of
our own for the typeof exemption on globals, window.X, the some-documents messages, and the fill-in exception, so it
would be an ESLint plugin of ours on top of es-x, against a standalone tool of about the same logic on acorn.

======================================================================
4. THE FOR-OF REWRITE
======================================================================

What @microsoft/msfs-ts-transformer 1.0.0 does (read in its transformer.js and README.md, from npm; measured by
running it through TypeScript 5.8.3's API with emit's before transformers, <scratch>/tsx5/run.cjs, strict on and off):
- Its peer dependencies are ts-patch ^3.3.0 and typescript ^5.8.3; it needs TypeScript's type checker
  (program.getTypeChecker()), so esbuild, which has no types, can't run it, and TypeScript 7.0, which ships no API,
  can't either (documented above).
- For-of: a for-of whose initializer is one declaration or an expression, not for await, whose body is a block, an
  expression statement, or empty, over a type with a number index signature and a length assignable to number,
  becomes:
    for (let _i_1 = 0; _i_1 < arr.length; ++_i_1) { const x = arr[_i_1]; ... }
  An iterated expression that isn't an identifier is first held in const _arr_N, so it runs once.
  Rewritten in our run: number[], arr.filter(...), Float64Array, string, readonly number[], and [string, number][].
  A string becomes an index loop, which yields UTF-16 code units where for-of yields code points, so a string holding
  a character outside the Basic Multilingual Plane iterates differently (measured output).
  Left as for-of: Map, map.values(), Set, a generator, an any-typed value, and a for-of whose body is an unbraced if.
  for await is left to TypeScript, which lowers it at es2017 with its __asyncValues helper.
- Array destructuring without rest and without defaults, over a number-indexed type, becomes indexed reads: variable
  declarations (const a = arr[0], b = arr[1]), parameters (moved into the body as let, unless a later parameter's
  default names one), assignments whose right side is an identifier, and the binding of a for-of over an iterable of
  indexable values: for (const [k, v] of map) became for (const _arr_2 of map) { const k = _arr_2[0], v = _arr_2[1]; },
  which stays a for-of over the Map. That last case applied only with strict on: with strict off, the iterator's
  return type is any and the transformer left the destructuring.
  Left: const [c, ...rest] = arr, const [d = 1, e] = arr, and spread [...arr], for which it has no case.

The published framework and our bundle (measured, <scratch>/cgt/forof.mjs, counting ForOfStatement nodes and
ForStatement nodes whose index is named _i_N):
  File                      | for-of | for await | _i_N loops | for-of from
  --------------------------+--------+-----------+------------+-------------------------------------------
  msfssdk.js 2.3.3          | 140    | 0         | 109        | 47 of the framework's build files
  whole.js (every export)   | 140    | 0         | 109        | the framework, all 140
  banner.js (FSComponent)   | 94     | 0         | 53         | the framework, all 94; 0 from our example
- So the published msfssdk.js already holds the transformer's output, and bundling it with esbuild keeps it.
- Its remaining for-of loops iterate what the transformer can't index: Sets (for (const key of this.backingSet)),
  Maps and their .values() (for (const repo of this.repos.values())), generators (for (const segment of
  this.segments()), for (const leg of plan.legs(...))), and Maps destructured into _arr_N (for (const _arr_1 of
  this._eventCache), from EventBus.js).
- Our own TypeScript compiled by esbuild keeps every for-of we write, over arrays included.
  esbuild's helpers add for-of of their own when our code uses object spread or rest at es2017: __spreadValues and
  __objRest each run a for (var prop of __getOwnPropSymbols(...)) loop on every call (measured in esbuild's output).
  banner.js has neither helper, since the framework's published JS, which parses at 2017, has no object spread or rest
  left for esbuild to lower.

Measurements of for-of in Coherent GT: none found (searched 2026-10-18).
- The transformer's README says for-of iteration "is not well-optimized by CoherentGT's Javascript interpreter or
  compiler" and that classical loops are always faster, and gives no numbers (documented by Working Title, no
  measurement).
- Coherent Labs' performance guide for GT calls its JavaScript engine an interpreter and says nothing of loops,
  iterators, or JIT (documented, coherent-labs.com/Documentation/cpp-gt/d9/df1/performance_guide.html).
- Searches of devsupport.flightsimulator.com, forums.flightsimulator.com, and the web for for-of, iterators, and
  Coherent turned up threads on the CoherentGTUI thread's cost per frame and on MSFS 2024 costing more than 2020 for
  the same gauges, none naming a loop construct (unverified forum reports, not measurements).
- A web search naming FlyByWire found nothing on it either, and our sibling repositories hold no such measurement
  (searched the FS Copilot fork's record/ and fsc-editor's docs/ for for-of and the transformer's name).
Decision 030's frame-time probe of the EFB app and the banner, built with the rewrite and without, still settles it.

======================================================================
5. SOURCE MAPPING
======================================================================

Measured with bad.ts (<scratch>/cgt/bundle-bad.mjs, check.mjs):
- esbuild writes the map with sourcemap: "external" (no //# sourceMappingURL comment in the bundle) or "linked"
  (with the comment); the check looks for <file>.map beside the bundle, or follows the comment.
- source-map-js 1.2.2: new SourceMapConsumer(JSON.parse(map)), then originalPositionFor({ line, column }), with
  column 0-based as acorn's loc.column is, and synchronous.
- Every failure in bad.js mapped to the TypeScript we wrote:
    54963:15  new RegExp("(?<y>\\d{4})-(?<m>\\d{2})")  -> ../example/bad.ts:8:13, the regex literal
    54967:18  .flat                                  -> ../example/bad.ts:13:16
    54967:25  .at                                     -> ../example/bad.ts:13:23
    54970:9   ResizeObserver                          -> ../example/bad.ts:17:7
  The minified bundle, 5 lines, mapped the same 4 to the same places (4:659250 and so on).
- esbuild read msfssdk.js's own //# sourceMappingURL=msfssdk.js.map and chained it: banner.js's map names 460 sources,
  459 under ../node_modules/@microsoft/build/ and ../example/banner.tsx, with sourcesContent.
  The framework's map points at its compiled build/*.js (459 sources such as ../build/data/BasicConsumer.js), not at
  its TypeScript, so a failure in the framework names its compiled file and line, and the path esbuild resolves,
  node_modules/@microsoft/build/, isn't a folder on disk; the check should print it relative to the package.
- sourceContentFor(source) gives the line's text to print beside the position.
- Cost: 58ms to build the consumer and do the first lookup on bad.js's 5.6 MB map, and 2ms for 1,000 more lookups.

======================================================================
UNVERIFIED AND OPEN
======================================================================

- What for-of costs in Coherent GT: no measurement exists that we found; decision 030's frame-time probe settles it.
- Whether a use can run before a package's own fill-in in an esbuild bundle (exception rule 4).
- Whether the engine lacks each later built-in the reference doesn't name (findLastIndex, trimEnd, toReversed,
  Object.groupBy, Promise.withResolvers); adding them to p09 and its next run settles it.
- Whether the engine parses a raw U+2029 (the reference says likely); acorn at 2017 rejects it either way.
- How many false positives our own code would add by name (ArrayUtils.at, StringUtils.trimStart,
  warning.description) before exception rule 3; counting them needs our code.
- es-x's resolution of constant variables in RegExp arguments was read, not run.
